title: london stocks rebound crude retreats ahead us inflation data 2026 09 11
text:
Sept 11 (Reuters) - London's FTSE 100 inched up on ​Friday, after five sessions of declines, as oil prices retreated on reports ‌of a push for a Strait of Hormuz deal, while markets awaited crucial U.S. inflation data, due later in the day.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE)
, opens new tab
 rose 0.45% to 10,656.78 ​points by 1006 GMT, but was on track for its biggest weekly loss since early July. ​The midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC)
, opens new tab
 gained 0.36% and was poised for its ⁠sharpest weekly decline in over four months.
